impulseguard

february 2026 · Ibtikar Case Competition, Waterloo

A browser extension MVP that detects add-to-cart actions, classifies purchases with the Claude API, and introduces a 24-hour cooling-off period.

I built the MVP in under 48 hours. Our team placed fourth among 32 teams at Ibtikar, presenting the technical architecture and monetization model to venture capitalists and industry investors.

a pause before checkout

The prototype explores how a browser extension can create space between seeing a product and buying it. On the supported site, BestBuy.ca, it identifies products and add-to-cart controls, uses Claude to classify a purchase as a need or want, and intercepts blocked purchases with a transparent overlay.

Blocked items remain on a 24-hour timer. The interface provides loading states and feedback during analysis, while the underlying product listing remains intact. The prototype's classification prompt leans toward blocking when uncertain.

how it works

  • XPath selectors locate products and add-to-cart buttons on supported shopping pages.
  • The Claude API considers product context rather than relying only on keywords.
  • chrome.storage.local persists blocked items and timestamps for the cooling-off rule.
  • Duplicate prevention keeps repeated interceptions from double-counting the same purchase.
  • A dashboard shows estimated savings, weekly totals, blocked purchases, detected and resisted impulses, and a success rate.

built with

React and TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, the Claude API, Chrome Manifest V3, and Chrome Storage. The interface uses emerald green and gold, with accessible Radix components.

what comes next

BestBuy.ca is the current supported store. The roadmap includes more stores, adjustable sensitivity, category preferences, spending alerts, budget integration, savings export, and shared impulse patterns. These are proposed extensions, rather than shipped features.
